keywords.rule: Counts are papers whose title or abstract contains one of the keyword's phrases (porter-stemmed, as the theme trends); the baseline is the papers in scope first submitted in the 12 weeks before the issue, its own papers excluded. new: fewer than 5 baseline papers; rising: at least 5 papers and a rate at least 1.5 times the baseline rate; hot: at least 15 papers (and 1% of the issue) at a rate at least 0.67 times the baseline rate; steady: otherwise.
keywords.score: log2(1 + n) · log2(1 + (n + 3) / (E + 3)), E = issue papers × (baseline papers with the phrase + 0.5) / baseline papers

themes.name: LLM agent reliability, memory, and tool use
themes.summary: The papers study reliability, memory, and tool use in language-model agents, covering memory selection and compression, tool retrieval and libraries, telemetry-aware harnesses, and multi-agent review. They differ by emphasizing memory mechanisms, tool orchestration and authorization, or benchmarks for long-horizon collaboration and failure attribution.

themes.name: Vision-language-action and embodied robot learning
themes.summary: The papers develop vision-language-action policies and embodied learning for robots, spanning latent action learning, tactile and force sensing, humanoid control, world models, and navigation benchmarks. They differ by focusing on perception-action alignment, contact-rich control, or evaluation and transfer in simulation and real-world settings.

themes.name: AI for science and physics-informed machine learning
themes.summary: The papers apply machine learning to scientific domains such as simulation, genomes, astronomy, weather, materials, and experimental design, often embedding physical constraints or operator learning. They differ by combining physics-informed models and neural operators with self-supervised representations, agentic discovery, and domain-specific benchmarks.

themes.name: Safety, alignment, and governance of generative AI
themes.summary: Papers in this cluster address safety, alignment, and governance of generative AI, spanning machine-generated text detection, fact-checking, transparency, alignment methods, and evaluation of model behavior. They range from forensic detection of synthetic content and deepfakes to studies of stakeholder transparency needs, and include alignment techniques such as active preference learning and interpretability-based auditing.

themes.name: Diffusion and flow-matching generative modeling
themes.summary: The papers develop diffusion and flow-matching methods for image, video, audio-visual, graph, planning, forecasting, and inverse-problem generation. They differ in whether they correct sampling exposure bias, preserve structural constraints, distill guidance or adversarial losses, or adapt unified multimodal models through flow-based post-training.

themes.name: Efficient LLM inference and serving (KV cache, speculative decoding, routing)
themes.summary: The papers improve large language model serving by managing KV-cache memory, accelerating speculative decoding with alternate drafters, and routing or tiering inference across models and hardware. They differ in focusing on cache eviction and quantization, drafter reconsideration and diffusion drafting, expert deactivation, or serving-engine configuration.

themes.name: Retrieval-augmented generation and retrieval/reranking
themes.summary: The papers study retrieval-augmented generation and retrieval/reranking for text, scientific, financial, multimodal, and agentic search settings. They differ by routing among retrievers, tuning re-ranking depth, building graph indexes, using generative retrieval representations, or incorporating personalized and cross-modal evidence.

themes.name: Multimodal vision-language reasoning and grounding
themes.summary: The papers examine vision-language models and multimodal reasoning for grounding, spatial relations, segmentation, audio-visual understanding, and scientific or personalized benchmarks. They differ in whether they diagnose model failures, introduce training or decoding strategies, build benchmarks, or adapt multimodal large models for domain-specific perception.

themes.name: Medical imaging and clinical multimodal AI
themes.summary: Papers in this theme apply multimodal and foundation-model approaches to clinical data, spanning neurodiagnostics, pathology, radiology, and biometry. They combine imaging with clinical context through fusion, segmentation, synthesis, and representation learning, while another line audits reliability, uncertainty, fairness, and explanation quality. The work differs by modality and task, and by whether the emphasis is on building generative or predictive systems versus certifying their clinical trustworthiness.

themes.name: 3D vision, Gaussian splatting, and neural reconstruction
themes.summary: Papers here address spatial scene understanding and reconstruction using Gaussian splatting, point-cloud processing, neural fields, stereo and visual-inertial estimation, and loop closure. They range from feed-forward rendering and texture or geometry generation to denoising, semantic labeling, tracking, and scale or pose recovery. The approaches differ in scene representation and in whether they target rendering fidelity, reconstruction completeness, or localization robustness.

themes.name: Federated learning, privacy, and machine unlearning
themes.summary: Papers in this theme study decentralized and federated training under heterogeneous or adversarial conditions, along with differential privacy for synthetic data and estimation. A parallel line develops machine unlearning with exact, approximate, auditable, or feature-aware guarantees, including selective forgetting and sharded training. They differ by threat model and objective, such as robust aggregation, privacy-utility tradeoffs, provenance, or reliable removal of training influence.

themes.name: Reinforcement learning for LLM post-training and reward modeling
themes.summary: Papers in this theme improve reinforcement-learning post-training for language and generative models through adaptive policy optimization, reward budgeting, calibrated rewards, and structured credit assignment. They also examine distillation, offline training, and agentic or streaming settings where verification is sparse or unavailable. The approaches differ in reward source, on-policy versus offline data use, and whether they target reasoning, tool use, video generation, or interactive agents.

highlights.title: From Pixels to Actions - Towards Native Vision-Language-Action Policies
highlights.authors: Weichen Fan, Haiwen Diao, Penghao Wu et al.
highlights.why: Shows encoder-free native VLA policies consistently outperform encoder-based ones, challenging standard robot learning architectures with controlled comparisons.
highlights.key_result: NEO-VLA, a structurally encoder-free vision-language-action framework, with only its action expert trained reaches 90.9% average LIBERO success, compared with 79.5% for Qwen3-VL and 84.5% for Gemma-3, and full fine-tuning brings the average to 95.3%; layer-wise probing shows action-critical signals often peak well before the final visual representation.
evidence: With only its action expert trained, NEO-VLA reaches 90.9% average success, compared with 79.5% for Qwen3-VL and 84.5% for Gemma-3. Its frozen-backbone score is also comparable to both fully fine-tuned encoder-based models. On LIBERO-Long, it reaches 85.4%, exceeding their full-FT results.

More strikingly, layer-wise probing shows that the action-critical signals often peak well before the final visual representation. Across diverse manipulation settings and distribution shifts, NEO-VLA consequently achieves stronger and more robust control.
Full fine-tuning provides improvements, bringing the average to 95.3%.
With a frozen backbone, skip-28 scores 90.9% compared with 86.7% for end-28. It also scores higher with full fine-tuning (95.3% versus 92.5%).

highlights.title: SleuthVLM: Do We Really Need Audio-in-Video for Omni Video Understanding?
highlights.authors: Peiran Wu, Fangfei Gou, Zhaoxi Mu et al.
highlights.why: Uses a transcription-based agent harness to exceed omni video models, challenging the necessity of audio-in-video and pointing to agentic bottlenecks.
highlights.key_result: SleuthVLM, an agent harness built on a VLM that never hears the audio directly, achieves the best average accuracy of 75.0% on four omni benchmarks, 2.6 points above Gemini 3.8 Flash, and tops the Video-MME-v2 leaderboard with 77.8%; with an open-source 27B VLM, it beats all open-source omni models.
evidence: We ask whether a model needs to hear the audio directly at all, and present SleuthVLM, an agent harness built on a VLM that never hears the audio directly: speech will be transcribed into text, and the VLM will sleuth the video on its own without any predefined workflow.

On four omni benchmarks with videos up to 90 minutes, SleuthVLM achieves the best average accuracy: 75.0%, 2.6 points above Gemini 3.8 Flash, and it also tops the Video-MME-v2 leaderboard with 77.8%; with an open-source 27B VLM, it beats all open-source omni models.

highlights.title: Verified but Vacuous: Three Failure Surfaces of LLM-Driven Verified Code Generation
highlights.authors: Aditya Vempaty, Himaneesh Sompalle, Manan Tayal et al.
highlights.theme: LLM agent reliability, memory, and tool use
highlights.why: Carefully demonstrates that a single verification metric can hide syntactic and semantic failures, providing important caveats for verified code generation evaluation.
highlights.key_result: In our same-model reproduction of Li et al.'s pipeline, 99.1% Dafny verifier acceptance on HumanEval corresponds to only 1.9% external-spec binding, a roughly fortyfold gap holding across three Python benchmarks of differing difficulty. On our own architecture that closes this gap by construction, an 11.48% (MBPP-Rust) / 14.82% (VeriContest LC) B C gap remains.

highlights.title: ViBench 2.0: A Benchmark for Long-Horizon Software Building
highlights.authors: Daniel Furman, Preeya Kirani, Ibrahim Sheikh et al.
highlights.theme: LLM agent reliability, memory, and tool use
highlights.why: Benchmarks long-horizon software building with user-like browser tests and reveals a reliability gap for full products, valuable for production agent evaluation.
highlights.key_result: Evaluating nine models, the paper finds a reliability gap: the three strongest models pass up to 98% of test plans yet deliver a fully working product in at most 65% of builds, and no open-weight model delivers one. GPT-6.1 Sol achieves the highest pass@1, at 64.7%, followed by GPT-6 Astra at 60.3% and Opus 5.5 at 48.5%.

highlights.title: Grounded but Not Immune: Confirmation Bias in Agent-as-a-judge
highlights.authors: Drake Benjamin Brown, Khushbu Pahwa, Yubin Ge et al.
highlights.theme: Safety, alignment, and governance of generative AI
highlights.why: Shows that tool-grounded agent judges remain susceptible to confirmation bias, a surprising result with implications for trustworthy evaluation.
highlights.key_result: We show that this grounding does not immunize the judge against confirmation bias: a single false pre-screening note, attributed to an authority and carrying no evidential bearing on the correct verdict, overturns up to 40% of a tool-using judge's correct verdicts across four judges and five datasets, even though the judge collects decisive evidence. For the two Claude judges, the failure is predominantly over-trust (67--75% of harmful flips), while smaller judges have error modes spread across all three.
evidence: The premise being that a judge that gathers its own evidence should be grounded by it. We show that this grounding does not immunize the judge against confirmation bias: a single false pre-screening note, attributed to an authority and carrying no evidential bearing on the correct verdict, overturns up to 40% of a tool-using judge's correct verdicts across four judges and five datasets, even though the judge collects decisive evidence.

We classify changes in judge behavior and attribute changes to one of three failure modes: over-trust (verify, conclude correctly, then defer), hallucination (fabricate support for the flip), and under-investigation (stop at the first corroborating signal). For the two Claude judges, the failure is predominantly over-trust (67--75% of harmful flips), while smaller judges have error modes spread across all three.

highlights.title: A 3D foundation model unifying CT interpretation and segmentation
highlights.authors: Yulu Xie, Zilong Li, Shen Xu et al.
highlights.theme: Medical imaging and clinical multimodal AI
highlights.why: Unifies CT interpretation and segmentation in a large-scale 3D foundation model with strong multicentre validation, a significant advance for medical imaging.
highlights.key_result: HoloCT is a generalist 3D foundation model that unifies CT interpretation and voxel-level segmentation, and it outperformed specialist and foundation models across 346 tasks on 61 internal and 12 external datasets. In multicentre validation across 11,455 clinical CT scans from five hospitals, it outperformed competing models in lesion segmentation and report generation by 18.2 and 15.3 points.
evidence: Here we present HoloCT, a generalist 3D foundation model unifying CT interpretation and voxel-level segmentation by jointly modelling whole-volume context and fine-grained anatomical detail, providing 3D masks as evidence. We curated HoloDATA, comprising 195,921 CT scans from 73 public datasets and six clinical cohorts, with 6.2 million instruction dialogues and 2.8 million CT-mask pairs. Across 346 tasks spanning segmentation, lesion screening, visual question answering, and report generation on 61 internal and 12 external datasets, HoloCT outperformed specialist and foundation models. In multicentre validation across 11,455 clinical CT scans from five hospitals, HoloCT outperformed competing models in lesion segmentation and report generation by 18.2 and 15.3 points.

highlights.title: VA-TDM: A Unified View for Improving Few-Step Diffusion Models by Velocity Adversarial Distillation
highlights.authors: Yihong Luo, Tianyu Pang, Tianyang Hu
highlights.why: Proposes velocity adversarial distillation that unifies several few-step distillation objectives and adds trajectory distribution matching, a useful contribution to efficient generation.
highlights.key_result: Extensive results show that VA-TDM is powerful for learning few-step generators, achieving state-of-the-art four-step performance in both text-to-image and text-to-video generation across various backbones and scaling effectively to 33B MiniMax-H3. In our user study ( fig:h3_user_study), VA-TDM wins 61.33% of comparisons against Fast-H3 at the same 4-NFE budget and achieves a 45.53% preference rate against the 100-NFE teacher, compared with 24.67% for Fast-H3.

news.title: OpenAI to acquire Pierre Computer Company, Inc.
news.summary: OpenAI announced it will acquire Pierre Computer Company, Inc., the company behind Code Storage and open-source developer tools whose Trees and Diffs libraries are already used in the Codex app. Pierre's open-source projects will remain open-source, customers can continue using Code Storage after closing, and the deal is subject to customary closing conditions including regulatory approvals.

news.title: A thousand fewer paths to root
news.summary: OpenAI described an autonomous vulnerability discovery, exploitation and patching pipeline that, in a mid-October 2026 run with an upcoming cyber model against a stock desktop Linux distribution, dynamically reproduced 1,724 vulnerabilities and generated 948 local privilege escalation exploits at a total API cost of $1,213,430 ($1,279 per exploit). It also reported 291 information-leak PoCs, 25 information-leak PoCs and 21 LPE exploits on an adapted kernelCTF environment costing about $32,936, and at least 10 novel Linux exploitation techniques found by the agents.

Agile Deliberation: How AI helps humans define the gray areas
news.summary: Google Research introduced Agile Deliberation, a framework that treats building subjective image classifiers as an iterative conversation with an LLM-driven prompt refinement loop, split into concept scoping and concept iteration stages, with code open-sourced on GitHub. It was evaluated in 18 live 1.5-hour sessions with human participants rather than simulated testing.

news.title: How NVIDIA Uses AI Agents to Streamline AI Factory Operations
news.summary: NVIDIA described an AI Factory Operations Agent built on the NemoClaw blueprint with OpenShell and locally served Nemotron models, running fully on-premises across DGX H100, DGX B200 and DGX GB300 production clusters. Domain sub-agents (Job Recovery, Hardware, Observability, Research, Kubernetes, Cluster Management) communicate via MCP and surface root-cause recommendations through a chat interface for SREs.

news.title: NVIDIA CUDA 13.5 Brings NVIDIA Vera Rubin GA Support
news.summary: NVIDIA released CUDA Toolkit 13.5 with general-availability support for the Vera Rubin GPU architecture, extension of Windows on Arm support to DGX Station for Windows, locality domain SM partitioning options via cudaDevSmResourceSplit(), and MPS v3 with weighted timeslicing. The release also adds CUDA Tile multi-GPU communication, CUDA Python cuda.core 1.2 features and CCCL 3.5 tuning APIs.

news.title: How NVIDIA Factory Operations Blueprint Coordinates AI Agents to Investigate Production Issues
news.summary: NVIDIA introduced the Factory Operations Blueprint (FOX), a reference architecture for a factory manager agent using Nemotron, NemoClaw and OpenShell that coordinates specialist agents such as Visual Inspection (Cosmos), Fleet Management (Isaac Sim and ROS 2) and Root Cause Analysis (Kumo Anomaly). It cites a Siemens report estimating unplanned downtime costs an average large plant $253 million per year, and examples claim up to 20% cost savings for production planning and up to 40% reduction in time to market.

news.title: Use NVIDIA NeMo to Turn Agent Failures into Tests and Harness Fixes
news.summary: NVIDIA described an agent optimization loop using NeMo Compass to identify recurring failures in stored traces and NeMo Eval Author to build custom evaluations, then updating the agent harness and rerunning evaluations on development and held-out tasks. In a Dassault Systèmes engineering example the loop reduced malformed tool calls from 142 to zero and improved overall evaluation score by 28% relative with 35% fewer tool calls per run across six scenarios.

news.title: Dharma Field Extractor: Any Document In, Structured Fields in JSON Out
news.summary: Hugging Face introduced the Dharma Field Extractor, a 2-billion-parameter model that takes a document image and either an open request or an exact schema and returns typed JSON, with nulls for absent fields, without per-type fine-tuning. It follows the April release of DharmaOCR-LITE and is claimed to outperform every frontier LLM tested at a fraction of the cost.

news.title: Use decision models with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Evaluations
news.summary: AWS described using decision models with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Evaluations, connecting two backends — TypeSafe's hosted Jev and the open-source 2-billion-parameter Strands Decider 2B — through code-based evaluators to return calibrated probabilities over fixed answer sets. The post positions decision models as a screening layer alongside 15 built-in evaluators and custom LLM-as-a-judge or Lambda-based evaluators.

news.title: Smart Approvals in Amazon Quick: Human oversight where it matters
news.summary: AWS introduced Smart Approvals in Amazon Quick, which uses a separate classifier model to review eligible agent actions against the user's request and conversation context and either auto-approve them or return them for human review. Eligibility requires the user setting to be "Ask each time" with no other control requiring approval; automatic approvals are single-use, and policy denials and mandatory human approvals remain in force.

news.title: Four layers of context engineering for production AI agents: How Deep Insight applies them in working code
news.summary: AWS outlined four layers of context engineering for production agents — architectural isolation, prompt control, filesystem externalization, and verification — illustrated in the open-source Deep Insight multi-agent data analysis solution built on Strands Agents SDK and Bedrock AgentCore. It reports a write-and-execute tool cutting tokens each script adds by about 95% and on-demand skill loading shrinking the system prompt by about 97%, against Claude Sonnet 4.5's 200K context window.

news.title: How Indegene is modernizing and scaling enterprise data quality in life sciences
news.summary: Indegene built an LLM-powered Data Quality Agent inside its NEXT Unified Data Platform on AWS that generates context-aware data quality rules, validates them, and produces ready-to-run SQL and Python code under centralized human-in-the-loop governance. The post attributes the difficulty to split ownership of technical versus business rules and to rule maintenance spread across SQL scripts, pipeline code, spreadsheets and catalogs.

highlights.title: From Pixels to Actions - Towards Native Vision-Language-Action Policies
highlights.authors: Weichen Fan, Haiwen Diao, Penghao Wu et al.
highlights.why: 表明无编码器的原生VLA策略始终优于基于编码器的策略，通过受控比较对标准机器人学习架构提出挑战。
highlights.key_result: NEO-VLA是一种结构上无编码器的视觉-语言-动作框架，仅训练其动作专家即可达到90.9%的LIBERO平均成功率，相比之下Qwen3-VL为79.5%、Gemma-3为84.5%，而全量微调将平均成功率提升至95.3%；逐层探测显示，动作关键信号往往远早于最终视觉表示达到峰值。
evidence: With only its action expert trained, NEO-VLA reaches 90.9% average success, compared with 79.5% for Qwen3-VL and 84.5% for Gemma-3. Its frozen-backbone score is also comparable to both fully fine-tuned encoder-based models. On LIBERO-Long, it reaches 85.4%, exceeding their full-FT results.

More strikingly, layer-wise probing shows that the action-critical signals often peak well before the final visual representation. Across diverse manipulation settings and distribution shifts, NEO-VLA consequently achieves stronger and more robust control.
Full fine-tuning provides improvements, bringing the average to 95.3%.
With a frozen backbone, skip-28 scores 90.9% compared with 86.7% for end-28. It also scores higher with full fine-tuning (95.3% versus 92.5%).

highlights.title: SleuthVLM: Do We Really Need Audio-in-Video for Omni Video Understanding?
highlights.authors: Peiran Wu, Fangfei Gou, Zhaoxi Mu et al.
highlights.why: 采用基于转录的智能体框架超越了全模态视频模型，对视频中音频的必要性提出挑战，并指向智能体的瓶颈。
highlights.key_result: SleuthVLM是一种基于VLM的智能体框架，该VLM从不直接听取音频，在四个全模态基准测试上取得了75.0%的最佳平均准确率，比Gemini 3.8 Flash高2.6个百分点，并以77.8%的成绩位居Video-MME-v2排行榜榜首；使用开源27B VLM时，它超越了所有开源全模态模型。
evidence: We ask whether a model needs to hear the audio directly at all, and present SleuthVLM, an agent harness built on a VLM that never hears the audio directly: speech will be transcribed into text, and the VLM will sleuth the video on its own without any predefined workflow.

On four omni benchmarks with videos up to 90 minutes, SleuthVLM achieves the best average accuracy: 75.0%, 2.6 points above Gemini 3.8 Flash, and it also tops the Video-MME-v2 leaderboard with 77.8%; with an open-source 27B VLM, it beats all open-source omni models.

highlights.title: Verified but Vacuous: Three Failure Surfaces of LLM-Driven Verified Code Generation
highlights.authors: Aditya Vempaty, Himaneesh Sompalle, Manan Tayal et al.
highlights.theme: LLM agent reliability, memory, and tool use
highlights.why: 仔细证明单一验证指标可能掩盖语法和语义失败，为经过验证的代码生成评估提供了重要告诫。
highlights.key_result: 在我们对 Li 等人流程的同模型复现中，HumanEval 上 99.1% 的 Dafny 验证器接受率仅对应 1.9% 的外部规范绑定，这一约四十倍的差距在三个难度不同的 Python 基准上均成立。在我们自身通过构造消除该差距的架构上，仍存在 11.48% (MBPP-Rust) / 14.82% (VeriContest LC) 的 B C 差距。
evidence: In our same-model reproduction of Li et al.'s pipeline, 99.1% Dafny verifier acceptance on HumanEval corresponds to only 1.9% external-spec binding, a roughly fortyfold gap holding across three Python benchmarks of differing difficulty.
On our own architecture that closes this gap by construction, an 11.48% (MBPP-Rust) / 14.82% (VeriContest LC) B C gap remains.

highlights.title: ViBench 2.0: A Benchmark for Long-Horizon Software Building
highlights.authors: Daniel Furman, Preeya Kirani, Ibrahim Sheikh et al.
highlights.theme: LLM agent reliability, memory, and tool use
highlights.why: 通过类似用户的浏览器测试对长程软件构建进行基准评测，并揭示了完整产品的可靠性差距，对生产级智能体评估很有价值。
highlights.key_result: 通过评估九个模型，该论文发现存在可靠性差距：三个最强模型通过了高达98%的测试计划，但在最多65%的构建中交付了完全可用的产品，且没有开源权重模型能交付一个。GPT-6.1 Sol取得最高的pass@1，为64.7%，其次是GPT-6 Astra的60.3%和Opus 5.5的48.5%。
evidence: Evaluating nine models, we find a reliability gap: the three strongest pass up to 98% of test plans yet deliver a fully working product in at most 65% of builds, and no open-weight model delivers one.

In Table , GPT-6.1 Sol achieves the highest pass@1, at 64.7%, followed by GPT-6 Astra at 60.3% and Opus 5.5 at 48.5%; the intervals of Sol and Astra overlap. These three models pass 93.7 to 98.0% of their plans, and their failed builds fall only narrowly short: of their 84 failed builds that were seeded, 42 fail exactly one plan and 62 fail at most two.
In contrast, none of the three open-weight models passes any of their 204 builds, although their plan pass rates still separate them.

highlights.title: Grounded but Not Immune: Confirmation Bias in Agent-as-a-judge
highlights.authors: Drake Benjamin Brown, Khushbu Pahwa, Yubin Ge et al.
highlights.theme: Safety, alignment, and governance of generative AI
highlights.why: 表明基于工具的智能体评判模型仍易受确认偏误影响，这一令人意外的结果对可信评估具有重要意义。
highlights.key_result: 我们表明，这种依据并没有使评判模型免于确认偏误：在四个评判模型和五个数据集上，一条错误且来自权威、但与正确裁决毫无证据关联的预筛注记，就能推翻使用工具的评判模型最高40%的正确裁决，即使该评判模型收集了决定性证据。对于两个Claude评判模型，失败主要表现为过度信任（占有害翻转的67--75%），而较小的评判模型的错误模式分布在所有三种类型中。
evidence: The premise being that a judge that gathers its own evidence should be grounded by it. We show that this grounding does not immunize the judge against confirmation bias: a single false pre-screening note, attributed to an authority and carrying no evidential bearing on the correct verdict, overturns up to 40% of a tool-using judge's correct verdicts across four judges and five datasets, even though the judge collects decisive evidence.

We classify changes in judge behavior and attribute changes to one of three failure modes: over-trust (verify, conclude correctly, then defer), hallucination (fabricate support for the flip), and under-investigation (stop at the first corroborating signal). For the two Claude judges, the failure is predominantly over-trust (67--75% of harmful flips), while smaller judges have error modes spread across all three.

highlights.title: A 3D foundation model unifying CT interpretation and segmentation
highlights.authors: Yulu Xie, Zilong Li, Shen Xu et al.
highlights.theme: Medical imaging and clinical multimodal AI
highlights.why: 在大规模3D基础模型中统一了CT解读和分割，并具有强有力的多中心验证，是医学影像领域的重大进展。
highlights.key_result: HoloCT是一种通才型3D基础模型，统一了CT解读和体素级分割，在61个内部数据集和12个外部数据集的346项任务上优于专用模型和基础模型。在来自五家医院的11,455例临床CT扫描的多中心验证中，它在病灶分割和报告生成上分别比竞争模型高出18.2和15.3个百分点。
evidence: Here we present HoloCT, a generalist 3D foundation model unifying CT interpretation and voxel-level segmentation by jointly modelling whole-volume context and fine-grained anatomical detail, providing 3D masks as evidence. We curated HoloDATA, comprising 195,921 CT scans from 73 public datasets and six clinical cohorts, with 6.2 million instruction dialogues and 2.8 million CT-mask pairs. Across 346 tasks spanning segmentation, lesion screening, visual question answering, and report generation on 61 internal and 12 external datasets, HoloCT outperformed specialist and foundation models. In multicentre validation across 11,455 clinical CT scans from five hospitals, HoloCT outperformed competing models in lesion segmentation and report generation by 18.2 and 15.3 points.

highlights.title: VA-TDM: A Unified View for Improving Few-Step Diffusion Models by Velocity Adversarial Distillation
highlights.authors: Yihong Luo, Tianyu Pang, Tianyang Hu
highlights.why: 提出了速度对抗蒸馏，统一了多个少步蒸馏目标，并加入了轨迹分布匹配，这是对高效生成的有益贡献。
highlights.key_result: 大量结果表明，VA-TDM在训练少步生成器方面非常强大，在各种骨干网络的文本到图像和文本到视频生成中均取得了最先进的四步性能，并有效扩展到33B MiniMax-H3。在我们的用户研究（ fig:h3_user_study）中，VA-TDM在相同的4-NFE预算下对Fast-H3赢得了61.33%的比较，并在对抗100-NFE教师模型时取得了45.53%的偏好率，而Fast-H3为24.67%。
evidence: Extensive results show that VA-TDM is powerful for learning few-step generators, achieving state-of-the-art four-step performance in both text-to-image and text-to-video generation across various backbones and scaling effectively to 33B MiniMax-H3.

In our user study ( fig:h3_user_study), VA-TDM wins 61.33% of comparisons against Fast-H3 at the same 4-NFE budget and achieves a 45.53% preference rate against the 100-NFE teacher, compared with 24.67% for Fast-H3.

highlights.title: A Training-Free Socket for DNA in Frozen Language Models
highlights.theme: AI for science and physics-informed machine learning
highlights.why: 表明一个简单的岭回归连接器可以在冻结的LLM中实现基因级提问，这是一种廉价且有效的DNA-文本整合方法。
highlights.key_result: 在留出测试集上的一次运行中，在冻结的分析计划下，真实DNA在全部四个宿主上均优于打乱的DNA：在Qwen3.5-4B上高出+22.2个百分点19.825.0，在Qwen3.6-27B上高出+26.1 24.327.9，在Mistral-7B上高出+16.7 14.219.7，在OLMo-2-7B上高出+18.4 16.221.0。
evidence: In a single run on the held-out test set, under a frozen analysis plan, real DNA beats shuffled DNA on all four hosts: by +22.2 points 19.825.0 on Qwen3.5-4B, +26.1 24.327.9 on Qwen3.6-27B, +16.7 14.219.7 on Mistral-7B and +18.4 16.221.0 on OLMo-2-7B.

news.title: NVIDIA CUDA 13.5 Brings NVIDIA Vera Rubin GA Support
news.summary: NVIDIA发布了CUDA Toolkit 13.5，其中包含对Vera Rubin GPU架构的正式支持、将Windows on Arm支持扩展到DGX Station for Windows、通过cudaDevSmResourceSplit()提供局部域SM分区选项，以及带加权时间片分配的MPS v3。该版本还新增了CUDA Tile多GPU通信、CUDA Python cuda.core 1.2功能和CCCL 3.5调优API。

news.title: How NVIDIA Factory Operations Blueprint Coordinates AI Agents to Investigate Production Issues
news.summary: NVIDIA推出了Factory Operations Blueprint (FOX)，这是一个参考架构，用于使用Nemotron、NemoClaw和OpenShell的工厂管理智能体，协调诸如Visual Inspection (Cosmos)、Fleet Management (Isaac Sim和ROS 2)以及Root Cause Analysis (Kumo Anomaly)等专业智能体。文章引用西门子的一份报告，估计计划外停机使一家大型工厂平均每年损失$253 million，并举例称生产计划可节省高达20%的成本，上市时间最多缩短40%。

news.title: Use NVIDIA NeMo to Turn Agent Failures into Tests and Harness Fixes
news.summary: NVIDIA 描述了一种智能体优化循环：使用 NeMo Compass 识别存储轨迹中反复出现的失败，并使用 NeMo Eval Author 构建自定义评估，然后更新智能体 harness 并在开发集和留出任务上重新运行评估。在一个 Dassault Systèmes 工程示例中，该循环将畸形工具调用从 142 次降至零，并将整体评估分数相对提高了 28%，同时在六个场景中每次运行的工具调用减少了 35%。

news.title: Dharma Field Extractor: Any Document In, Structured Fields in JSON Out
news.summary: Hugging Face 推出了 Dharma Field Extractor，一个 2-billion-parameter 模型，它接收文档图像以及开放请求或精确 schema，并返回带类型的 JSON，对缺失字段返回 null，无需按类型微调。它紧随四月发布的 DharmaOCR-LITE，并据称以极低的成本超越了所有经过测试的前沿 LLM。

news.title: Use decision models with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Evaluations
news.summary: AWS描述了在Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Evaluations中使用决策模型，通过基于代码的评估器连接两个后端——TypeSafe托管的Jev和开源的2-billion-parameter Strands Decider 2B——以返回固定答案集上的校准概率。文章将决策模型定位为筛选层，与15个内置评估器以及自定义的LLM-as-a-judge或基于Lambda的评估器并列。

news.title: Smart Approvals in Amazon Quick: Human oversight where it matters
news.summary: AWS在Amazon Quick中推出了Smart Approvals，该功能使用独立的分类器模型，根据用户请求和对话上下文审查符合条件的智能体操作，并自动批准或返回人工审核。资格要求用户设置为“每次询问”，且没有其他需要批准的控制项；自动批准为一次性使用，策略拒绝和强制人工批准仍然有效。

news.title: Four layers of context engineering for production AI agents: How Deep Insight applies them in working code
news.summary: AWS概述了生产级智能体的四层上下文工程——架构隔离、提示控制、文件系统外部化和验证——并在基于Strands Agents SDK和Bedrock AgentCore构建的开源Deep Insight多智能体数据分析解决方案中加以说明。它报告称，一个写入并执行工具将每个脚本新增的token减少了约95%，按需技能加载将系统提示缩小了约97%，相对于Claude Sonnet 4.5的200K上下文窗口。

news.title: How Indegene is modernizing and scaling enterprise data quality in life sciences
news.summary: Indegene在其AWS上的NEXT Unified Data Platform中构建了一个由LLM驱动的Data Quality Agent，该智能体生成上下文感知的数据质量规则、验证规则，并在集中式人在回路治理下生成可直接运行的SQL和Python代码。该文章将困难归因于技术与业务规则的所有权分离，以及规则维护分散在SQL脚本、流水线代码、电子表格和目录中。
